thread:
omar: Alert from anomaly-detector: auto-downgrade trigger fired for route `file-parser` in eu-west at 02:04 UTC. It flipped policy to permissive and attached 300 sample rejects. Customers reported "tool error".

kesha: Wait, auto-downgrade ran? I thought we only had auto-observe for canaries. Is this new behavior?

deploy-bot: auto-downgrade: route=file-parser region=eu-west policy=permissive reason=reject_rate>0.15 triggered_by=anomaly-detector at=02:04:12 UTC samples_attached=300

omar: Looks like the anomaly-detector rule is live under infra/auto-safety and signed off last month. It was meant to protect customers but we didn't discuss audit/visibility. We need a quick postmortem if this changes customer experience.

sylvie: Two problems: 1) attackers could spam malformed tool outputs to force permissive, bypassing enforcement 2) the Console has no clear UI for auto-changes so support can't see why a route suddenly softened.

ops: For immediate mitigation I'm disabling auto-downgrade for prod regions and leaving observe-only. Command: `infractl rules disable auto-safety.auto-downgrade --env production`

deploy-bot: rule.disabled: auto-safety.auto-downgrade env=production requested_by=ops 02:12:07 UTC

kesha: Good. Longer-term proposals: a) require multi-signal voting for auto-downgrade (reject_rate > threshold AND fallback_rate > threshold AND not_from_untrusted_origins) b) per-account impact guard: if >5% of affected requests come from a single external account, block auto-downgrade and page us. c) add a cooldown window to prevent flip-flopping.

omar: Also console changes: show a new audit stream for automated policy changes and label them clearly (actor=automation vs human). Make samples accessible with redaction and a link to the triggering signals.

sylvie: Telemetry asks: add `auto_change` boolean tag to validator metrics, include `trigger_signals` list (comma-separated string) and `affected_account_dist` (top2 accounts). Make reject_rate published as rejects/requests to make thresholds meaningful.

ops: Safety: implement allowlist for trusted internal agents that can trigger auto-downgrade; block untrusted external origins. Add a manual override flag `allow_auto_action=true` on selected routes only.

kesha: UX: Console should surface auto-change candidates in a "Pending Auto Actions" drawer for 5 minutes before application, giving on-call a chance to abort. That gives us human-in-the-loop for dubious cases. Also make sample size configurable per-route.

omar: For alerts, page when either: hard_reject_rate > 0.08 for 3m OR auto-downgrade executed AND affected_customers_count > 1. That prevents noisy paging for single-account issues.

sylvie: Also propose soft-reject responses carry `x-redwood-validation: soft_warning` header plus a structured `validation` field in JSON when callers request `?verbose=true` so integrations can surface actionability.

ops: I'll file infra-10800 (disable auto-downgrade in prod, add multi-signal voting and allowlist), infra-10801 (console: auto-action audit + pending drawer), infra-10802 (telemetry tags & reject_rate ratio), infra-10803 (per-account impact guard). Assigning infra-10801 -> console-zoe, infra-10802 -> kesha, infra-10800 -> ops, infra-10803 -> sylvie.

console-zoe: I'll mock the pending drawer and audit stream as a feature-flagged panel. We should show triggering signals and a single-click abort.

omar: Thanks. We'll reconvene after infra tickets land. If anyone sees customer billing spikes hold the permissive toggle and page.

sylvie: One more ask: add an integration with runbooks so auto-actions include a runbook link in the audit entry. Saves time when paging.

omar: Great suggestion. Adding to infra-10801.

ops: rule: auto-downgrade will remain disabled in production until we deploy the voting/allowlist changes. We'll run a retro on the detector thresholds and docs.

omar: Closing loop: I'll send a short incident note to #incidents if we confirm any user-facing billing or SSE impact. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
